$comment: The top-level public surface of toolnexus, as defined by SPEC.md §1–§11. This manifest is the single source of truth for the API Reference: it drives page generation, the sidebar, cross-language equivalent links, and the coverage gate. One entry here == one page per port at /api/<lang>/<group>/<member>. Data shapes (option bags, result records) are NOT entries — they are documented as field tables on the page of the entry point that consumes them. Add an entry only when SPEC.md gains a top-level entry point.

entries.title: Tool — the one interface
entries.summary: The uniform shape every tool source collapses to: name, description, JSON-Schema parameters, execute.

entries.title: ToolResult — what execute returns
entries.summary: The result envelope: output text, optional error flag, optional Pending for suspension.

entries.title: ToolContext — what execute receives
entries.summary: Optional per-call context handed to execute: cancellation, identity, and host-supplied state.

entries.title: createToolkit — the aggregator
entries.summary: Collapse MCP servers, skills, built-ins, A2A agents and your own functions into one tool list.

entries.title: loadMcp — connect to MCP servers
entries.summary: Read an mcp.json, connect every local stdio and remote streamable-HTTP server, expose each server tool as a Tool.

entries.title: loadMcpWithContext — cancellable load
entries.summary: The ctx-aware load: bound connection time and cancel a slow or hung server without leaking a child process.

entries.title: listMcpTools — inventory without connecting
entries.summary: List what each configured server would expose, plus per-server status, without wiring it into a toolkit.

entries.title: parseMcpConfig — validate an mcp.json
entries.summary: Parse and validate config without connecting — the fast fail for a malformed or misspelled server block.
entries.parityNote: Java keeps parseConfig package-private (McpSource.java:141) — there is no public config parser. C# exposes it as McpSource.ParseConfig, not ParseMcpConfig.

entries.title: Elicitation bridge — server asks the user
entries.summary: Map an MCP server's elicitation request onto the §10 suspension contract, and map the answer back.
entries.parityNote: Elixir's elicitation_to_request lives on Toolnexus.Mcp.Protocol, not Toolnexus.Mcp — there is no delegate on the top-level Mcp module.

entries.title: loadSkills — discover SKILL.md files
entries.summary: Glob a skills directory and expose one skill tool with progressive disclosure.

entries.title: loadSkillsWith — data skills, providers, filters
entries.summary: Supply skills as data or from a lazy provider, and narrow them per agent with an allowlist.

entries.title: listSkills — inventory and skip reasons
entries.summary: Enumerate discovered skills and, crucially, the ones that were skipped and why.

entries.title: defineTool — your own function as a tool
entries.summary: Wrap a plain function with a name, description and schema — the shortest path from code you have to a tool the LLM can call.

entries.title: Annotation / reflection tools
entries.summary: Derive the schema from the function signature or annotation instead of writing it by hand.
entries.parityNote: Elixir has no reflection-based tool builder; use Toolnexus.Native.define_tool/1 with an explicit input_schema.

entries.title: collectTools — gather decorated functions
entries.summary: Sweep a module or class and collect every function marked as a tool.
entries.parityNote: JS/Java/C# expose an explicit collector; Python, Go and Elixir have no equivalent public symbol.

entries.title: httpTool — a REST endpoint as a tool
entries.summary: Turn an HTTP endpoint into a tool: URL, method, headers with ${ENV} expansion, and a schema.

entries.title: selectBuiltins — choose the shipped tools
entries.summary: Pick which built-in file/shell/web tools are in play, by name or by source toggle.
entries.parityNote: Elixir selects built-ins via Toolnexus.Builtin.load/1 (a config map), not a named select function.

entries.title: createBuiltinTools — the full built-in set
entries.summary: Construct every built-in tool directly, outside a toolkit.
entries.parityNote: Elixir has no Builtin.create/1 — the zero-arg 'build the full set' constructor is Toolnexus.Builtin.tools/0.

entries.title: toOpenAI — emit OpenAI tool schema
entries.summary: Render the toolkit as OpenAI function-calling schema.

entries.title: toAnthropic — emit Anthropic tool schema
entries.summary: Render the toolkit as Anthropic tool-use schema.

entries.title: toGemini — emit Gemini tool schema
entries.summary: Render the toolkit as Gemini function-declaration schema.

entries.title: createClient — the tool-calling loop
entries.summary: The unified client: system prompt, skills injection, parallel and chained tool calls, retries, memory.

entries.title: run — one turn of the loop
entries.summary: Send a prompt, let the loop call tools until the model stops, get a RunResult.

entries.title: stream — token and event streaming
entries.summary: The streaming loop: text deltas, tool-call events, and suspension events as they happen.

entries.title: Hooks — lifecycle middleware
entries.summary: Intercept before/after model calls and tool calls: audit, redact, veto, or rewrite.
entries.parityNote: Elixir has no separate Hooks type — pass a :hooks map (:before_llm, :after_llm, :before_tool, :after_tool) to Toolnexus.Client.create/1.

entries.title: Conversation — multi-turn memory
entries.summary: Keep a transcript across turns so the model remembers what it already did.

entries.title: ConversationStore — durable transcripts
entries.summary: Swap in-memory history for your own store so a conversation survives a process restart.

entries.title: onMetric — observability
entries.summary: Emit one metric event per model call and per tool call: tokens, latency, outcome.

entries.title: Retries, timeout, cancellation
entries.summary: Classify an LLM error into retry / fail, bound a run with a deadline, and cancel cleanly.
entries.parityNote: Elixir configures retries/timeout as options on Toolnexus.Client.create/1 rather than a distinct error-classifier type.

entries.title: agent — call a remote A2A peer
entries.summary: Point at a remote agent's card and use it exactly like a local tool.

entries.title: agentTools — a peer's skills as tools
entries.summary: Expand a remote agent card into one tool per advertised skill.

entries.title: parseAgentsConfig — agents from config
entries.summary: Declare remote peers in config the way MCP servers are declared, with precedence rules.

entries.title: serve — expose your toolkit as an A2A agent
entries.summary: Publish an Agent Card and answer JSON-RPC over the client loop — your toolkit becomes someone else's remote agent.

entries.title: buildAgentCard — describe yourself to peers
entries.summary: Construct the Agent Card that advertises your name, skills and endpoint.

entries.title: TaskStore — durable inbound tasks
entries.summary: Persist inbound A2A tasks so a suspended request survives a restart.

entries.title: buildMcpServer — expose your toolkit over MCP
entries.summary: The inbound MCP profile: any MCP client can call your tools.

entries.title: Agent — a composable sub-agent
entries.summary: Define a sub-agent with its own toolkit, prompt and budget, callable as a tool by its parent.

entries.title: AgentRuntime — spawn, wait, interrupt
entries.summary: The six host verbs that drive sub-agents, plus the read-only list and inspect views.

entries.title: Handle — a running sub-agent
entries.summary: The state machine for one spawned agent: pending, running, suspended, done.

entries.title: Budgets — hierarchical, live-enforced
entries.summary: Cap tool calls and wall-clock per agent and per team, enforced while the run is in flight.

entries.title: The task tool — model-facing delegation
entries.summary: The opt-in tool that lets the model itself spawn a teammate. Default OFF.
entries.parityNote: Only JS exposes a constructible task tool symbol; elsewhere it is the `task` builtin, toggled on the runtime.

entries.title: composeSoul — the directory is the agent
entries.summary: Build a persona's system prompt from its home directory: identity, memory, skills.

entries.title: fromDir — load a persona from disk
entries.summary: Point at an agent home directory and get a configured agent back.

entries.title: memoryTool — file-backed memory
entries.summary: The opt-in built-in that lets a persona write durable notes to its own home.

entries.title: compactor — keep a long run under budget
entries.summary: Summarise older turns when the transcript grows, so a long-lived agent stays inside its context window.

entries.title: pending — suspend and ask a human
entries.summary: Return a Pending from a tool to park the run until someone answers.
entries.parityNote: Elixir ships no pending/1 producer — construct %ToolResult{metadata: %{pending: %Request{}}} directly. Only the reader, ToolResult.pending?/1, exists.

entries.title: authRequired — suspend for authorization
entries.summary: The auth-shaped suspension: hand back a URL, resume once the user has granted access.
entries.parityNote: Elixir ships no auth_required/pending producer helpers — build %ToolResult{metadata: %{pending: %Request{}}} by hand. Only the reader, ToolResult.pending?/1, exists.

entries.title: waitFor — the one host slot
entries.summary: The single hook where the host resolves a suspension — in-process prompt or durable queue, same contract.
entries.parityNote: Elixir passes :wait_for as an option to Toolnexus.Client.create/1 rather than exposing a WaitFor type.

entries.title: pendingOf — read a suspension off a result
entries.summary: Detect that a RunResult is parked rather than finished, and get the Request that parked it.
entries.parityNote: Elixir has no pending_of/1; match on result.metadata or use ToolResult.pending?/1.

entries.title: Durable resume — answer across a restart
entries.summary: The answer-carrying entry point: resume a parked run in a different process.

entries.title: Relay tools — declaration-only
entries.summary: Declare a tool the host executes, not the library: the call rides out on the suspension.
entries.parityNote: Go-only today (golang/relay.go). SPEC §10 addendum landed as a Go preview; the other five ports do not ship a relay tool yet.

entries.title: translate — one turn, no loop
entries.summary: Declare a toolkit to a provider and translate one request/response without executing anything or keeping state.

entries.title: Inbound translation — transcripts across providers
entries.summary: Convert an OpenAI-shaped transcript into Anthropic shape, including the tool-result merging a flattening translator gets wrong.
entries.parityNote: Go keeps openAIMessagesToAnthropic unexported (golang/translate.go:283) — inbound translation is reachable only through Translate.
